packs.title: Newport’s houses, coast and collections
packs.promise: Separate estate, coast, fort and museum outings across Newport.

q.s: Read materials and arrangement in Marble House.
st: Enter the actually opened house visitor route with the required admission and choose three available material or spatial details.
For each, describe a visible material, scale or arrangement and paraphrase one relevant interpretation if supplied. Mark an unknown material as a question rather than guessing.
Compare two records: how does a different material or arrangement change the impression of the space? Keep your impression separate from a claim about historic intent.
Keep three detail notes and one comparison; no rubbing, tracing, close-up copying or decorative-art reproduction.

q.s: Connect an available collection item with its room.
st: Enter the actually opened museum with the required admission and choose an available interpreted collection item and one visible feature of the room around it.
Describe one detail of the item without reproducing its design, then paraphrase what its interpretation tells you. Record one separate spatial observation about the room.
Explain how the setting changes what you notice first. Identify which part comes from interpretation and which part is your observation.
Keep the two observations and connection; no particular object, upstairs room or garden bloom is required.

q.s: Compare observation and interpretation inside an opened museum.
st: Enter the actually opened general-admission galleries with the required ticket and select three available works or interpreted objects.
For each, write one visible formal observation and paraphrase a short relevant interpretive point when available. Do not copy the work, label or a recognizable decorative motif.
Compare two records: what did you see before reading, and what did interpretation add? Distinguish observation, source information and your response.
Keep three notes and a comparison; writing after leaving is equally valid.

packs.title: Newport’s historic streets and harbor
packs.promise: Two connected afternoons of Black history, a registered synagogue visit and distinct public street and harbor experiences.

q.t: Three links in Black Newport history
q.s: Read present interpretation in the Center for Black History.
st: Enter the actually opened center exhibition with the required admission and choose three available interpreted records, objects or stories concerning Black Newport history.
For each, paraphrase one point made by the center and record the type of evidence it uses. If a detail is uncertain, keep the uncertainty rather than inventing a connection.
Compare two records: what can each kind of evidence tell you, and what does it leave unanswered? Do not write as a historic person or reproduce sensitive records.
Keep three evidence links and one comparison; no particular object, family story or temporary exhibit is required.

q.s: Compare a civic building with its public square.
st: Choose three actual visible relationships between the Colony House and the square, such as a doorway facing an approach, a window rhythm or a change of scale.
Describe one specific feature in each relationship without copying inscriptions or a decorative emblem. Read the linked operator identity/history for context.
Compare two cues and distinguish a visible observation from the source’s account of the building. Keep three cue notes and one comparison.

q.t: Three links between a building and service
q.s: Connect an exterior with the Institute’s documented maritime role.
st: Observe two actual visible exterior features from a lawful public-sidewalk position without entering a doorway or service area.
Read the current operator account and paraphrase one documented maritime or community function. Do not infer a person’s circumstances from seeing them enter.
Write three links: two visible building details and the sourced service function, then explain what the exterior alone cannot establish.
